I made both versions. They are in `public/models/`, and each stays at or above the tool's "no visible quality loss" limit (fidelity 0.9 or higher).

| | original | `lantern-small.glb` | `lantern-gpu.glb` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Download | 9.56 MB | **0.221 MB** (−97.7%) | 1.526 MB (−84%) |
| GPU memory | 85.6 MiB | 21.5 MiB (−75%) | **3.1 MiB** (−96%) |
| Load on 4G (download plus decode) | 9.3 s | **0.36 s** | 2.4 s |
| Fidelity | – | 0.900 | 0.912 |
| Textures | 4× PNG 2048² | 4× AVIF 1024² | 4× KTX2 UASTC 768² |
| Decoder | – | meshopt (6 KB) | KTX2/Basis (260 KB) |

- **Small:** it is 7× smaller to download than the GPU version. It uses 7× more GPU memory (21.5 vs 3.1 MiB), because AVIF textures are decompressed to full size on the GPU.
- **GPU:** it keeps textures compressed on the GPU. It costs 1.3 MB more to download, and it loads about 2 s slower on 4G, mostly because of the 260 KB decoder and the transcode step.
- **Geometry:** both versions have the same 5,394 triangles. Geometry is only a few hundred KB, so the textures account for almost all of the savings.

- **Fidelity margin:** the small version sits right at the 0.9 limit, so there is little margin. The score is measured at 1024px. If the lantern will be shown large or in VR, I can re-tune at 2048px for a safer margin.
- **Browser support:** the small version needs a browser that supports AVIF. Babylon.js 7.10 or newer loads AVIF textures natively. Both decoders load automatically in Babylon.js.
- **Which to pick:** on a mobile or VR target that runs out of memory, pick the GPU version. For fast page loads, pick the small one. At 21.5 MiB, the small version is probably fine unless you have many lanterns on screen.

The tuning recipes and previews are in `recipes/`.
